name: Hit on the contact frame
definition: The transient of an impact sound sits on the frame where contact is visible (synchresis fuses them).
how: Place the SFX so its transient = contact_frame / fps. If it must move, move late (≤ +1 F), not early.
use_when: any contact: object lands, door shuts, punch, glasses placed
common_mistakes: placing the file start (with silence/lead-in) instead of the transient
check: Frame-step: waveform transient on the same frame as the visual contact.

sync_offset.ms_tolerance: detectable if sound leads > ~45 ms or lags > ~125 ms (broadcast speech)

tool_hint: sound.py: b.hit('name', t_contact, gain_db, pan=x) · soundtrack.py cue {t, file, gain}

name: Footsteps on contact frames
definition: One footstep per contact frame of the walk/run; pan follows screen position.
how: Take contact times from R.walk / walkSide step starts; vary 3–4 samples, pitch ±3%, heel-toe for slow walks.
purpose: Grounds characters in space; sells weight and surface.
avoid_when: very wide shots where feet are not visible and ambience covers
common_mistakes: steps drifting off contacts after a speed change
check: Mute music, watch feet: every contact has a step.

name: Whoosh peaks at the fastest point
definition: A whoosh's loudest moment aligns with the fastest frame of the move (or the smear), not with its start.
how: Find the peak in the waveform; place t = t_fastest − peak_offset.
use_when: whip pans, fast moves, transitions, smears
common_mistakes: aligning file start to motion start
check: Peak of the whoosh on the fastest/smear frame.

name: Riser ends on the cut
definition: A rising sound builds tension and ends exactly on the cut/reveal, followed by a hit or silence.
how: Start at cut − riser_duration; end on the cut frame; then hit or drop to silence.
use_when: before reveals, scene changes in promos
check: Last loud frame of the riser = cut frame.

name: J-cut (audio leads picture)
definition: The next shot's sound starts before its picture.
how: Lead ambience 0.3–0.6 s (repo convention); lead dialogue a few frames to ~1 s.
purpose: Pull the viewer into the next scene; smooth, invisible transitions.
use_when: location changes, someone about to speak, door bell before door
common_mistakes: lead too long (sound doesn't match picture any more)
check: Does the sound make you want to see its source?

name: L-cut (audio trails over the next picture)
definition: The previous shot's sound continues over the new picture (e.g., a line continues over the listener).
how: Hold dialogue/ambience 0.3–2 s into the next shot; cut picture to the reaction.
use_when: dialogue → reaction shot, ending a scene on a sound

examples.note: L = previous audio over new picture

common_mistakes: L-cut that hides an important line under new information
check: Picture changes while the line is still being heard.
tool_hint: cut picture earlier than the audio cue end

name: Room tone bed
definition: Continuous location 'silence' under dialogue; never digital zero inside a scene.
how: Loop room tone/ambience across all cuts in a location (−22 to −26 dB vs VO); crossfade 2–4 F at edits.
purpose: Makes edits and TTS gaps seamless; hides cuts.
avoid_when: deliberate silence moments (then duck, not delete)

examples.note: edit blindness mostly disappeared without audio

common_mistakes: ambience changing on every cut within one location
check: Listen at every cut: no holes.

name: Cut on the downbeat / phrase
definition: Major cuts land on bar downbeats or phrase starts (every 2–4 bars); minor cuts may land on beats.
how: frames_per_beat = fps*60/BPM; use real beat times (librosa beat_track) and round each to the nearest frame; never accumulate rounded beats.

examples.note: viewing differs between conditions; direction not read

common_mistakes: every single cut on the beat for > 10 s (mechanical)
check: Overlay beat grid: big cuts within ±1 F.

name: Off-beat cut for emotion
definition: Deliberately cut off the beat to let a reaction finish (emotion outranks rhythm).
how: Hold the shot until the reaction completes, then cut; keep music playing through.
purpose: Prevent the music grid from cutting emotions short.
use_when: reactions, emotional peaks inside musical montages
common_mistakes: cutting a reaction in half to hit a beat
check: Does the reaction finish before the cut?

name: Kinetic type on the beat
definition: Words appear on beats (one word/phrase per beat), entrance finished by the beat.
how: Start the entrance 2–4 F before the beat so the word is fully in on the beat; hold readable.
purpose: Drive and memorability for beat clips.
common_mistakes: entrance starting on the beat (lands late)
check: Word fully visible on the beat frame.

name: Stinger on the reveal
definition: A short musical/sound accent caught exactly on a reveal or punchline (a 'catch').
how: Transient on the reveal frame; often after a duck/silence.
common_mistakes: stinger + loud music at the same time (masking)
check: Duck music 3–6 dB under the stinger.

name: Silence before the reveal
definition: Pull everything down 0.5–1.5 s before a reveal or scare, then hit.
how: Duck all beds −12 to −20 dB (keep room tone faintly), then the hit/reveal.
check: Bed level drops before the reveal and returns with it.

name: Duck music under voice
definition: Music/ambience drop when the voice speaks.
how: Music −16 to −20 dB under VO (FX.md table); LD ≥ 10 LU music vs VO (MIX_PLAYBOOK); 150 ms ramps.
check: VO intelligible on a phone speaker.

name: Mickey-mousing
definition: Music imitates every movement (steps, falls, climbs).
how: Musical accents on every action beat; easiest with a fixed tempo click.
avoid_when: drama, serious brand content (reads as parody)
check: Is the imitation intended to be funny?

name: Play through (no catch)
definition: Music flows over events without hitting them, carrying a continuous mood.
how: Ignore minor hit points; align only phrase starts with scene starts.
use_when: montages of feeling, story clips under VO

examples.note: soundtrack alters interpretation of the same scene

common_mistakes: random accidental hits that feel like mistakes

name: Mouth leads audio by 1 frame
definition: On-screen mouth shapes lead the audio slightly; never shift the voice to fit the picture.
how: Mouth keys 1 F early; vowels ≥ 2 F; closures before /m b p/.

name: Off-screen sound tease
definition: A sound whose source is not yet visible, then revealed (often with a J-cut).
how: Quieter, darker (low-pass 2–4 kHz), wetter than on-screen; pan toward the source side; reveal on cut.
check: Character looks toward the sound before we see it.

name: Layered SFX (transient + body + tail)
definition: Build one event from 3–4 layers so it reads on phones and has material and space.
how: Transient on frame; body 0–1 F later; tail/reverb to room size; sub only for hero moments on good speakers.
check: Each layer audible solo and together.

name: Choose music for meaning, not only energy
definition: Music changes how viewers interpret ambiguous action; pick by intended meaning.
how: Test 2 music options on the key scene; ask viewers what will happen next.
